subject.title: fix(exec): bypass fail-closed interpreter heuristic when security is full

question: Should `security="full"` bypass the ambiguous-interpreter script-preflight rejection for approval-gated `ask="on-miss"` and `ask="always"`, or only for YOLO `ask="off"`?
rationale: The implementation is narrow, but this decides when OpenClaw skips a fail-closed exec preflight gate; code review cannot choose that operator trust boundary without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Accept full-security bypass
options.body: Treat `security="full"` as the trust gate regardless of ask mode, keep the updated docs/tests, and re-review the refreshed branch before merge.

options.title: Keep YOLO-only bypass
options.body: Preserve the current `security="full"` plus `ask="off"` contract and revise code/docs so approval-gated modes still fail closed on ambiguous interpreter commands.

options.title: Defer to the linked security issue
options.body: Pause this PR until the protected security-labeled issue receives an explicit maintainer policy decision.

recommendation.title: Accept full-security bypass
recommendation.body: Treat `security="full"` as the trust gate regardless of ask mode, keep the updated docs/tests, and re-review the refreshed branch before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest history owner for the current YOLO skip helper and approval docs that define the boundary being changed.
